youtube_title: Twin Lakes near Plymouth, 1838: the Potawatomi Trail of Death
body: In 1838, a militia marched more than 800 Potawatomi out of Indiana at gunpoint. It started at Twin Lakes, near Plymouth, where their leader, Menominee, had refused to give up his people's land. The governor sent General John Tipton and a volunteer militia. On September 4 the march began, with Menominee and two other leaders held under guard in a wagon, and the militia burned the village so no one could return. They traveled about 660 miles in 2 months, to what is now eastern Kansas. At least 42 people died on the way, many of them children. It became known as the Trail of Death. Today, markers follow the route across 4 states, and a statue of Menominee has stood near Twin Lakes since 1909.
